title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Goal Bonus and New-Money Promotional Rate
content:
Beyond base interest, certain tiers of the Savings & Money Market Accounts family pay one of two tier-specific extras: a goal bonus for a cycle of disciplined saving, or a promotional rate on new money during the first months after opening. This page defines when each is earned and on how much balance.

## Goal bonus

**Earned for a cycle** only on a tier whose goal rate is above 0.00, and only when both of these hold for the cycle:
- the net deposits of the cycle reach the tier's goal deposit level, where net deposits means the deposits posted in the cycle less the withdrawals posted in it, with interest credits, fees and fee refunds left out of both sides; and
- not a single withdrawal of any kind posted in the cycle. An overdraft protection transfer into checking is a withdrawal for this purpose, so any one of them costs the cycle its goal bonus.

**Once earned,** the goal rate covers each day of the cycle, on the part of each day's balance up to the tier's goal balance ceiling, and is credited as the goal bonus component.

## Promotional rate

**Applies** only on a tier that offers a promotional rate, only on days that fall within the promotional period, and only if the new money brought in reached the tier's new-money requirement.

**New money** is the total of deposits made at a branch, by check deposit, by mobile deposit, by ACH credit or by incoming domestic wire that posted from the opening date through the date that lies the tier's funding window of calendar days after it, both ends included. A transfer from another Piedmont Crescent Bank account, whether an internal transfer or an automatic transfer, is never new money.

**Promotional period.** Months are counted from the opening date. A day is inside the period when it falls on or before the date reached by adding the tier's promotional length, in calendar months, to the opening date; that date is the promotion end date held on the account. The end date itself is inside. Once that end date has passed, no share of the balance is promotional any longer: all of it is rated at the base yield, with the relationship bonus added where one is earned.

**Promotional share.** Each day, the part of the balance up to the tier's promotional balance ceiling is the promotional share, credited as the promotional component.

**Conversion.** If the account is converted to another tier, the promotional period ends on the conversion date.

**Late new money.** Money that arrives after the funding window does nothing toward the requirement, yet once the requirement has been met it does earn the promotional rate, within the ceiling.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical account opened 20 June on a tier with a six-month promotion)

| Day | Inside the promotional period? |
|---|---|
| 19 December | yes |
| 20 December, the end date | yes |
| 21 December | no, base interest and any relationship bonus only |

## Points of judgement

**A Goal Builder Savings cycle had strong deposits and one ATM withdrawal. Is the goal bonus paid?** No; any withdrawal in the cycle rules it out.

**Does a transfer in from the customer's own checking account help meet the new-money requirement?** No; money moved from another account at the bank is not new money.
